summary: Move F: 4-lens review of BIOS-004 surface + adversarial verification per finding
logs: 4 lenses reviewing; each finding goes straight to an adversarial skeptic

confirmed.claim: Concurrent useCompleteMission calls corrupt each other's optimistic UI: the second mutation's optimistic completion can be silently reverted by the first mutation's error rollback, because onError restores a previousData snapshot taken before the second mutation's optimistic write existed.
confirmed.fix: Scope the optimistic patch/rollback per-mission instead of swapping the whole cached list back to a stale full-list snapshot — e.g. on error, only revert the single goal this mutation touched (find-by-id and reset just its status/progress) rather than overwrit

confirmed.claim: The XP-delta diff for a mission completion is computed from a single shared, un-scoped `queryKeys.gamification()` cache entry with no concurrency guard, so two missions completed in quick succession can misattribute XP: the second mutation's postStats can include the first mutation's XP gain, inflat
confirmed.fix: Serialize completeMission calls (e.g. TanStack Query v5 mutation `scope`/queue, or a client-side in-flight lock keyed off queryKeys.gamification()) so two completions never diff against overlapping pre/post snapshots, or attribute XP server-side per-completion

confirmed.claim: mission.progress is rendered as a raw, unclamped percentage in text/KPI labels while ProgressRing internally clamps the same value to [0,100] for the visual arc, so out-of-range server progress (explicitly undocumented/unvalidated server-side) produces a ring that visually reads 100% next to a label
confirmed.fix: Clamp mission.progress once (e.g. in the adapter's toMissionsView, or a shared clampProgress helper) before it reaches any label/KPI formatter, so the ring, the hero centerLabel, GlassStatCard's 'Progress' tile (mission-detail-screen.tsx:255), and today-screen

confirmed.claim: The create-mission SegmentedTabs option labeled 'Main mission' can never actually produce a Main Mission (silver) tier badge — because this create surface always posts to the life-goals endpoint (source is always 'life' server-side) and mapTier resolves isPrimary+life to the 'life' (gold) tier befor
confirmed.fix: Either relabel the create-screen option (e.g. 'Life mission' / 'Side mission') to match the tier it will actually produce, or add UI copy/preview showing the resulting tier badge before submit, so users aren't told 'Main mission' and shown a 'Life Mission' bad

confirmed.claim: CIAPresenceOrb's state-transition effect only sets the shared values relevant to the newly-entered state and never resets the ones owned by the state being left, so switching state (idle/listening/thinking) at runtime leaves a previous state's withRepeat(-1) animation running indefinitely underneath
confirmed.fix: At the top of the effect (before the state-specific branches), reset every shared value not owned by the incoming state to its rest value (ringOpacity=0, ringScale=1, shimmerRotate=0 unless state==='thinking', etc.) so leftover withRepeat loops from a prior st

confirmed.claim: Selecting "Main mission" in the S15 create flow silently produces a gold-tier "Life Mission", not the silver "Main Mission" the UI just showed the user picking — a mislabeled RPG reward the user will see contradicted on every other screen.
confirmed.fix: Either (a) remove/relabel the S15 mission-type picker to reflect what the create surface can actually produce (life vs side only, since source is fixed to 'life' this batch), or (b) have mapTier/the create body distinguish an explicit 'main, non-primary-life'

confirmed.claim: ChipDomainTag — used on all five BIOS-004 screens for domain labeling — never renders CANON §4's mandated per-domain colors; it only supports a generic active(orange)/inactive(gray) binary, so every domain chip in the batch (Fitness, Wellbeing, Nutrition, Finance, Career, Learning, etc.) renders in
confirmed.fix: Add a DOMAIN_COLORS token map to constants/theme.ts (CANON §4 hex list) and thread a `domain` key into ChipDomainTag so it tints background/label per domain instead of the current binary active/inactive styling.

confirmed.claim: S14's KPIRow renders "Progress / Target / XP" instead of the canon/architecture-plan-mandated "Actions / Streak / XP", duplicating the hero ring's own value in the first slot instead of showing the documented honest-null for missing Actions/Streak data.
confirmed.fix: Render Actions and Streak KPI slots with `nullMetric(...)` honest-null copy (as the spec anticipates) instead of replacing them with "Progress" (redundant with the hero ring) and "Target".

confirmed.claim: Today's FABQuickLog is wired to push straight to mission-create, contradicting the architecture plan's own explicit contract that Today's FAB is visual-only this batch (only the Missions-board FAB is wired to create).
confirmed.fix: Make Today's FAB a non-interactive/visual placeholder (or route it to a real water/meal/mood quick-log surface) and reserve the mission-create navigation for the Missions board FAB only, per the architecture plan's own row-by-row contract.

confirmed.claim: Mission tier labels are capitalized inconsistently between screens ("Life Mission" Title Case on Mission Detail vs "Life mission" sentence case on the Missions board), violating canon's sentence-case rule and breaking exact-copy consistency for the same RPG term.
confirmed.fix: Delete the duplicate TIER_LABEL constant in mission-detail-screen.tsx and import/reuse `tierLabel()` from missions-board-logic.ts (or a shared module) so both screens render the same sentence-case string.

confirmed.claim: GlassStatCard's outer View sets a crafted accessibilityRole/accessibilityLabel but never sets `accessible`, so on iOS the label is never exposed as a single VoiceOver stop — the grouped summary falls apart into fragmented child reads across every metric card in the batch (Today vitals, Missions summ
confirmed.fix: Add `accessible` (or `accessible={true}`) to GlassStatCard's outer View (and to ActionCheckCard's outer View in mission-detail-screen.tsx), matching the pattern already used correctly in ChipDomainTag's static branch and LoadingState.

confirmed.claim: CIAInsightCard's content wrapper has the same missing-`accessible` defect as GlassStatCard, so the carefully-built `accessibilityLabel` ("Cia insight: ..." / "Cia insight, locked: ..." / the honest-null string) never reaches VoiceOver as a grouped announcement on Mission Detail or Celebration.
confirmed.fix: Add `accessible` to the `styles.ciaContent` View so the pre-built `accessibilityLabel` string (headline/body/gated/honest-null) is announced as one unit instead of leaking into per-child Text reads.

confirmed.claim: ActionRow's accessibilityLabel omits the domain, and because the row is a single accessible Pressable, the nested `ChipDomainTag` (which is separately marked `accessible`) is an orphaned nested-accessible child that VoiceOver never reaches — screen-reader users never learn which life domain a Today
confirmed.fix: Fold the domain into ActionRow's (and MissionPinRow's) accessibilityLabel string, e.g. `${label}, domain ${domainLabel}. ${done ? 'Completed' : 'Not yet done'}.`, and stop relying on the nested chip's own label to carry that information.

confirmed.claim: The bottom tab bar's pill and per-tab items use hard-coded `height` (not `minHeight`) around a Dynamic-Type-scaling label, so on larger accessibility text sizes the tab labels will clip or overflow the fixed 44px/60px containers on the one navigation surface present on every authenticated screen.
confirmed.fix: Switch `pill`/`item` to `minHeight` (with the icon+label column allowed to grow), or cap the label's font scale with `maxFontSizeMultiplier` so it stays legible without breaking the fixed pill chrome.

confirmed.claim: The celebration transparentModal's scrim never sets `accessibilityViewIsModal`, so VoiceOver's swipe navigation is not confined to the modal card — a screen-reader user can swipe past the Continue button and reach controls on the mission-detail/missions screen sitting behind the 82%-opacity scrim, w
confirmed.fix: Add `accessibilityViewIsModal` (iOS) to the top-level `styles.scrim` View so VoiceOver treats the celebration card as the only focusable content while it's on screen.

confirmed.claim: MomentumBar carries no accessibility semantics at all — no accessibilityRole, no accessibilityValue — unlike its sibling ProgressRing (same kit, same purpose) which correctly exposes `accessibilityRole="progressbar"` and `accessibilityValue`; VoiceOver users get nothing but whatever plain-text `labe
confirmed.fix: Give MomentumBar's container `accessibilityRole="progressbar"` and an `accessibilityValue={{ min: 0, max, now: value }}`, mirroring ProgressRing, instead of depending entirely on the optional `label` prop.

confirmed.claim: MissionRow's accessibilityLabel reports tier and progress but drops mission status (active/blocked/complete), even though a StatusChip is rendered visually right next to the tier badge — screen-reader users can't tell a blocked mission from an active one without opening it.
confirmed.fix: Append status to the row's accessibilityLabel, e.g. `..., status ${mission.status}`.

confirmed.claim: TrendChart's optional scrub interaction is implemented with raw touch responders and exposes only a static `accessibilityRole="image"` / `accessibilityLabel="Trend chart"`, with no `accessibilityRole="adjustable"` or accessibility actions — a VoiceOver user has no way to explore the underlying data
confirmed.fix: When `onScrub` is provided, switch the container to `accessibilityRole="adjustable"` with `accessibilityActions`/`onAccessibilityAction` (increment/decrement) stepping through points, and build the label from the actual data range.

confirmed.claim: The S42 celebration route is reachable via the app's registered custom URL scheme with no auth gate and no server round-trip, so a crafted deep link can make the app render a fully fabricated "+N XP · you earned it" reward screen styled with real-provenance chrome.
confirmed.fix: Do not trust raw URL params as the sole source for the reward number. Have `useCompleteMission`'s onSuccess mint a short-lived, unguessable in-memory token (e.g. a Zustand/ref-backed one-shot value) alongside the confirmed xpDelta, and have `CelebrationScreen`

confirmed.claim: `use-mission-mutations.ts` — the file implementing the batch's single highest-risk honesty computation (the pre/post gamification-stats XP diff) and the optimistic-update/rollback path — has zero unit test coverage anywhere in the repo, despite the accepted architecture plan explicitly mandating one
confirmed.fix: Add `use-mission-mutations.test.ts` per the plan: assert xpDelta is null when preStats is undefined/uncached, null when postTotal <= preTotal, a correct positive number when it increases; assert onMutate flips status/progress optimistically and onError rolls b

confirmed.claim: The XP-honesty delta is a global gamification-stats snapshot diff, not scoped to the specific mission being completed, so a second completion (or any other async XP event) landing inside the same pre/post refetch window can misattribute someone else's XP to the mission the user just tapped complete.
confirmed.fix: Document this as an accepted limitation (no server award-id exists to correlate against, per ADR-4), or narrow the window by capturing `preStats` synchronously right before firing the complete call rather than reusing whatever happens to already be cached from

refuted.claim: The CIA coach-card headline copy and its single Tiempos-italic emphasis word both deviate from the S12 spec and its own rendered screenshot.
